# FanumTag v0.1.0

The first FanumTag release delivers a local-first Windows workspace for generating
descriptive filenames without uploading personal media.

## Highlights

- Local Qwen3-VL image and meme captioning with stronger on-image text priority and
  character recognition.
- Image, video, audio, and text-file queues with thumbnails, filtering, pagination,
  selection tools, and safe bulk renaming.
- Responsive runtime controls, progress reporting, cancellation, and persisted
  automatic startup.
- Configurable Qwen and MMProj paths under **Settings → Runtime Settings**.
- Bundled llama.cpp, CUDA runtime dependencies, Whisper, and FFmpeg support in the
  packaged Windows distribution.

## Windows installation

A complete Windows package contains the setup executable and a neighboring
`weights` directory:

```text
FanumTag-windows-x64/
├── fanumtag_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe
└── weights/
    ├── Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf-00001-of-00002.gguf
    ├── Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf-00002-of-00002.gguf
    └── mmproj-F16.gguf
```

Keep this layout intact and run the installer from inside that folder. Setup checks
the three model files and copies them into the installed application. Moving the
installer away from `weights`, or downloading only the installer, causes setup to
stop with a missing-model message.

After installation, leave **Qwen Model Path** and **MMProj Model Path** empty to use
the bundled defaults. To use other compatible weights, select them with **Browse**
and click **Save Configuration**. Select the first file for a sharded Qwen model and
keep its remaining shards in the same directory.

The complete packaged distribution is approximately 3.44 GiB. This release was
published without rebuilding the deleted Windows build output, so its GitHub assets
currently contain source archives only. The automatic source archives do not include
the Git-ignored model weights or native runtime files.

## Verification performed before release

- Production frontend build passed.
- All 14 Rust tests passed.
- Qwen's two-shard model and MMProj loaded successfully in llama-server.
- The NSIS install and uninstall hooks compiled successfully in the last package
  validation performed before the build output was removed.
